function: Downlink CSI feedback in FDD massive MIMO: compression at the UE encoder and recovery at the gNB decoder, adaptable to new scenarios with few samples (pp. 1-3).
system: Nb=32 gNB antennas, single-antenna UEs, FDD OFDM; carriers 5.3 GHz, 300 MHz, 2.61 GHz, 2.6 GHz; no RIS (pp. 1, 2, 7).
method: Deep unfolding ISTA decoder (SPTM2-ISTANet+) with trainable measurement matrix; CSI-TransNet CNN plug-in translation modules trained per new scenario (transfer); supervised MSE loss; model-driven augmentation (pp. 3-7).
data_channel: COST 2100 indoor and outdoor, KU Leuven measured indoor CSI, QuaDRiGa 3GPP TR 38.901 UMa; training set 100,000 and testing set 20,000 (p. 7).
test_conditions: Pretrained on one dataset, tested on three unseen ones directly, with sparsity aligning, or after fitting translation modules on 200 or all new samples (pp. 9-10).
baselines: Learned CSI feedback: CsiNet+, DCRNet, STNet, TransNet, ISTANet+, TiLISTA-Joint; augmentation: ChannelGAN, flipping, rotation, PRS-guo22; direct reuse, retraining from scratch (pp. 8-9).
metrics: NMSE (dB) and cosine similarity of the recovered CSI at compression ratios 1/4 to 1/32 (p. 7).
complexity: Tables III-V (p. 12): SPTM2-ISTANet+ encoder 1.0 M parameters, 2.1 M FLOPs at CR 1/4; translation module 1.8 K parameters; Table VI gives augmentation cost.
openness: No code released; uses a public measured dataset, IEEE Dataport DOI 10.21227/nr6k-8r78 (ref. [34], p. 13).
q1_support: p. 7: "COST2100 model [33] with 5.3 GHz downlink frequency"; "the channel setting described in 3GPP TR 38.901" (QuaDRiGa UMa); "recorded from KU Leuven Massive MIMO testbed in" (measured data).
q2_support: p. 9: "three datasets unseen by the pretrained model as new scenarios." The pretrained model is reused directly or after a translation module is fitted on 200 samples (Aug200), across other carrier frequencies and subcarrier spacing (p. 10).
q3_support: p. 8: "We compare SPTM2-ISTANet+ with six known schemes", all learned (CsiNet+, DCRNet, ISTANet+, TiLISTA-Joint, TransNet, STNet). Not met: no classical or non-learned CSI feedback method (compressive sensing solver, codebook) is compared; flipping, rotation, and PRS-guo22 (p. 9) are training-data augmentations, not CSI feedback methods.
q4_support: p. 12: "TABLE IV: Computational complexity (FLOPs) of encoder networks in UE." Table III gives parameters, Table V runtime, and Table VI augmentation cost (p. 12).
q5_support: p. 7: "3) Measured Indoor. This dataset contains CSI samples" recorded on the KU Leuven testbed; p. 13: "https://dx.doi.org/10.21227/nr6k-8r78" (ref. [34], IEEE Dataport). The paper releases no code of its own.
notes: Area 2: the learned method compresses and recovers the downlink CSI; the augmentation module (channel synthesis for training) and the translation module serve this function. q3 is borderline: the only non-learned comparisons (flipping, rotation, PRS-guo22 versus the learned ChannelGAN, Fig. 7, p. 9) concern training-data augmentation, so the reviewer should confirm that they do not count. q5 rests on the public measured dataset, since no code link appears. The PDF is arXiv 2211.14785v2 (6 Nov 2023), titled Deep Learning for Efficient CSI Feedback in Massive MIMO: Adapting to New Environments and Small Datasets.
